data.text:
Linus Torvalds, creator of Linux and Git:

"Talk is cheap. Show me the code"

GLM-5.2 just hit #1 on Design Arena’s single-turn HTML Web Design eval

The useful read is the build recipe:

1. Start with the benchmark
   - single-turn HTML Web Design
   - non-agentic
   - user preference as the judge

2. Check the price
   - GLM-5.2: $1.40 / $4.40 per 1M tokens
   - Fable 5: $10 / $50 per 1M tokens

3. Use it where it won
   - landing pages
   - marketing pages
   - animated web concepts
   - rich first screens

4. Don’t force it everywhere
   - Fable 5 still ranks above it in Game Dev
   - Data Viz
   - 3D Design

5. Copy the dependency pattern
   - chart.js
   - three.js
   - TailwindCSS
   - font-awesome

6. Give it room to write
   - GLM-5.2 produced 25% more code text
   - avg generation time: 304.7 seconds
   - twice as long as Fable 5

7. Watch the length ceiling
   - article says 46K-57K characters was the sweet spot
   - past that, preference gains slow down

8. Review for template reuse
   - GLM-5.2 seems to have strong starting templates
   - good for average quality
   - risky if every client site starts looking related

9. Use it for first-pass frontend
   - let it generate the page
   - then audit layout, assets, speed, mobile, copy

The lesson: for web design, the winning model may be the one that ships a better default page before you touch the prompt twice

quotedTweet.text:
【保存版】

Karpathyがこう言った😳

https://t.co/qiHvwbLfyM

「ボトルネックから自分を外せ
レバレッジを最大化しろ
少ないトークンを入れるだけで
大量のことが自分の代わりに起きる」

これを構造で実現するのが「ループエンジニアリング」だ

手で回すセッションでは
「次に何を実行するか」と
「出力を確認するか」の2つを
人間がやっている

ループエンジニアリングは
この2つをシステムに移す

構造はこの4層👇

・スケジュール → 何を実行するかを決める
・ループ(メーカー) → 実際に作業する
・チェッカーエージェント → 出力を採点する
・ディスクのファイル → 2つが共有する状態を保持

設計のポイントが4つある

(1) チェッカーは別エージェントにする
モデルが自分の出力を採点すると
失敗を見つけるより正当化する方向に動く
チェッカーの結果が次のメーカーへの指示になり
何も見つからなくなるまでサイクルが回る

(2) 停止条件はループ前に設定する
実行中に変えるとトークンを燃やし続ける
シンプルな例：主要な問題を修正して最終パスを1回
「全テスト通過かつlintクリーン」で終了

(3) 状態はコンテキストではなくディスクに持つ
モデルは実行をまたいで記憶しない
MDファイルが「何が終わったか」「何が残っているか」を保持する
これで数日後にループが再開できる

(4) 検証バーが低いほど安全に動く
バージョン文字列の確認や不足テストの検出など
退屈で反復的な作業は人間が離れていても任せられる
判断が重いタスクも、チェッカーが結果を確認できる範囲ならループ化できる

Claude Codeのエージェントが途中で止まる原因の多くは
状態設計の問題だ

コンテキストに依存した状態は
セッションが切れた時点で白紙になる

チェッカー分離・停止条件の事前設定・ディスク状態の保持
この3つが整ったとき
Karpathyが言った「自分をボトルネックから外す」が初めて成立する

the latest run proves that open models are no longer just matching closed flagships - they are out-designing them.

- Three.js visual engine with sand, forest, and snow biomes

- working crafting table with plank recipes
- ore generation: coal, iron, gold
- underground cave networks + day/night cycle
- locked 60 FPS

the visual edge is clear:

GLM 5.2 handled complex window transparency that other models failed, outperforming ChatGPT 5.5, Kimi, and Claude Opus 4.8. it generated the visual environment in 20 minutes

the math vs logic trade-off:

Claude Fable 5 still wins on raw coding logic and stability (it has working sprint). but GLM 5.2 won on world generation, adding cave systems and mob drops nobody requested

the bugs in the code:

health indicators render behind the inventory panel, mined blocks teleport directly to slots, and hit zombies levitate

which model fits your stack better - the premium closed flagships or the cheaper open setups?

GPT-5.6 vs GPT-5.5 on my custom spaceship prompt.

I gave both models the exact same custom prompt. This is also the same prompt I previously gave to Fable 5.

For context, GPT-5.6 Pro worked for 87 minutes, while GPT-5.5 Extra High worked for 34 minutes and 42 seconds.

As I’ve said before, based on great authority GPT-5.6 will be an incremental/soldi improvement over GPT-5.5, not a “Fable killer.” My rough expectation has been that it would trade blows with Fable 5 on some benchmarks, maybe win around half depending on the category, but not clearly surpass it overall. And again fable five will have bigger model smell, but this was expected.

After testing this coding output, that view feels pretty accurate.

GPT-5.6 is clearly better than GPT-5.5 in several visual areas. The lighting, shading, chairs, object details, and exterior of the spaceship looked noticeably stronger. The scene was also easier to test.

I do want to give GPT-5.5 credit though. It built out the rooms much much better and the planets looked better than GPT-5.6’s. It was also interesting that both GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 produced better-looking planets than Fable 5 in this specific test.

The downside with GPT-5.5 was stability. The game was much glitchier and harder to test compared to GPT-5.6.

But when it comes to the core of the demo, which is the spaceship itself, Fable 5 still beat both models pretty comfortably. GPT-5.6 is impressive, but from this test, it looks exactly like what I expected which was a meaningful incremental improvement over GPT-5.5, at least for indie game demos, but not something that replaces Fable 5.

In collaboration with @chetaslua

Officially, I do not see GPT‑5.6 or GPT‑5.6 Pro announced yet. OpenAI’s current public model list still highlights GPT‑5.5 / GPT‑5.5 Pro as the latest top GPT‑5.5 line, and OpenAI’s release notes currently show GPT‑5.5-related updates rather than a GPT‑5.6 release. So the safe framing is “expected,” “rumoured,” “from what I’m hearing,” “early tests suggest,” not “is coming” unless you are intentionally presenting yourself as a source.

Best strategic framing

The deeper story is not:

GPT‑5.6 is better at 3D but still weak at frontend.

The better story is:

GPT‑5.6 may be another step toward spatial/visual agents, but not yet the model that solves product taste.

That is much more interesting. It creates a clean split:

Where GPT‑5.6 may be advancing: spatial reasoning, 3D scene construction, SVG/geometry, image-to-structure, asset generation, technical visual tasks.

Where it may still lag: frontend taste, hierarchy, responsive polish, interaction details, state design, product judgment, and browser-verified refinement.

The real thesis:

The model may be getting much better at constructing objects, but not yet at designing products.

That is a strong line.

Quick grammar and credibility fixes

Original:

GPT 5.6 and 5.6 Pro is coming in a few days.

Better:

GPT‑5.6 and GPT‑5.6 Pro are expected in the next few days.

Safer:

GPT‑5.6 / GPT‑5.6 Pro are expected soon, possibly within days.

Most credible:

From what I’m hearing, GPT‑5.6 / GPT‑5.6 Pro may be only days away. Still unconfirmed until it appears in OpenAI’s release notes, the model picker, or API docs.

Use GPT‑5.6, not GPT 5.6. Use are, not is.

The Fable comparison needs careful handling

“Surpassing even Claude Fable 5” is a very strong claim. Anthropic describes Claude Fable 5 as its most capable model for ambitious coding projects, long-running agentic work, high-fidelity design implementation, and vision-assisted checking. That means saying GPT‑5.6 surpasses it in any area should be framed as domain-specific, not global.

Also, there is a current availability wrinkle: Anthropic announced Fable 5 and Mythos 5 on June 9, 2026, but later said a U.S. government directive required it to disable access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers. So comparisons should be phrased as comparisons against known Fable 5 performance/tests, not necessarily against a currently accessible product.

Better:

In early tests, GPT‑5.6 appears to beat Fable 5 in some narrow visual/spatial tasks, especially 3D-style asset generation and structured geometry.

Even better:

I would not say it beats Fable 5 overall. But in some 3D/spatial-generation tasks, GPT‑5.6 looks surprisingly strong — maybe stronger than Fable in that lane.

Best:

The interesting part is not that GPT‑5.6 is “better than Fable.” It is that it may beat Fable in a specific category where OpenAI has not always led: spatial construction.

Fix “3D modeling”

“3D modeling” is ambiguous. People may think you mean professional CAD, Blender workflows, mesh topology, UV unwrapping, rigging, texture baking, or game-ready assets.

Be precise.

Use one of these:

3D scene generation
3D-style asset generation
Three.js scene construction
Blender scripting
SVG/geometry generation
spatial layout and object construction
procedural 3D prototyping
3D mockup generation from prompts
Best version:
In 3D-style scene construction and procedural asset generation, it looks much stronger than GPT‑5.5 — and in some narrow tests, even stronger than Fable 5.
That avoids overclaiming professional 3D modelling mastery.
Fix “frontend issues”
“Frontend issues” is too vague. Name the failure modes.
Possible issues:
weak visual taste
generic SaaS layouts
poor spacing rhythm
fragile responsive states
inconsistent typography
bad component hierarchy
accessibility gaps
weak animation judgment
shallow design-system use
overdecorated dashboards
poor empty/error/loading states
failure to inspect rendered output
code works, product feels off

Suggested wording:

The disappointing part is frontend. It may write cleaner code, but it still seems to struggle with the parts that matter most in real product work: taste, spacing, hierarchy, responsive behaviour, interaction states and design-system consistency.

That is much better than “frontend issues.”

Strongest rewritten version

data.text:
順便一提。

想測試一個模型是否真正具備 Fable 5 「長時程自主完成複雜任務」的能力，最簡單直接的實驗場景是：

請模型把「你現實中最想去的具體地點」做成一個美觀、有氛圍的 three.js 互動虛擬景觀網頁。

要求：
- 玩家可以用滑鼠/鍵盤自由移動、旋轉視角
- 有適當的光影與大氣效果
- 場景要能傳達出該地點的真實氛圍

以上基本能一次验证 Anthropic 官方强调的 Fable 5 所有核心能力。

因爲 Fable 會自主研究真實地點，找到這個地點所有相關的數據，再去做創意轉化 + 技術實現，一次造出高质量的作品。其他模型暫時都不能做到~

quotedTweet.text:
當我們在用 Fable 5 的時候，我們到底在用什麼？

昨天試著讓 Opus 4.8 接力把這東西修下去，結果人差點累廢了（😇

幾乎通宵，把 X 上流傳的、想讓 Opus 4.8 像 Fable 5 那樣超長工作的方法都跑了一遍，比如Pliny 發的那份所謂洩露的 system prompt，還有好些人試的提煉 session，全試了…… 之前忙於如何實現工具，沒有思考過更底層的問題，因此也算對 A 社的產品多了點理解。

btw Pliny 那份洩露的是 Chat / App 的系統提示詞，不是 agentic 腳手架那套，拿來讓 Opus 做長程 agent 工作完全不靠譜，這東西靠譜用法還是 Pliny 沒直接公開的多 agent 解構／重組工作流，搞越獄。

反正，結論是：（至少對這種大型複雜任務）都沒用。

靠有限的時間和訊息，試圖把強模型的行為一致性歸納出來，做成外部工程，想讓弱模型逼近強模型，對這種要長時間把控全局的任務，完全不現實。

同一個任務，Fable 5 能長時間獨立做完、幾乎不用人介入；換成上面這些方法讓 Opus 4.8 來硬凑，耗時十幾倍起步，錯誤百出，只能靠人腦不斷介入、統籌全局。

歸根到底，這兩個模型在把控空間的全局一致性上，能力差異是天壤之別。Fable 5 就是強太多，沒話説。

「用 Opus 在 100 小時內能完成的工作，用 Fable 可以在 1 小時內完成。」—— 這麽説，一點也不誇張。

Fable 本質是一種新 agent 工作流範式，新的 agent 工作流範式，意味著使用者要用新的思考方式去對待任務，不管以後還能不能用，好歹是提前體驗了一把未來一部分該有的樣子，知道該往哪些方向繼續卷了~
